text:
liz: quick sync — i sketched a short playbook for decoupling the runtime adapter surface between hosted/dedicated/private. want to validate tradeoffs before i turn it into an RFC.

omar: thanks. can you paste the sketch here? curious about the auth and manifest handling bits.

liz: sure — high level: 1) split runtime-adapter surface into Core (runtime calls, qkv/kv cache ops) + Orchestration (manifest translation, routing, auth glue). 2) define a compact handshake proto between Core <-> Orchestration that only includes: model_id, seq_len_hint, kv_capabilities, preferred_kernels, auth_token_type. 3) Add a compatibility layer that translates old adapter fields to the new handshake for 6 months. 4) Migration plan: canary on dedicated, opt-in on private, feature-flag rollout hosted.

kai: i like the Core/Orchestration split. question: does Core need to know about tenant auth at all? i'd prefer zero auth surface in Core and have orchestration inject credentials into a secure channel.

liz: agreed — Core should be auth-agnostic. the handshake only signals auth_token_type (eg: none/jwt/kms). the actual token exchange happens over a short-lived mTLS sidechannel we call "agent-token-proxy".

maria: one caveat: the ML runtime needs to allocate kv cache differently for private vs hosted because of multi-tenant memory accounting. how do we communicate that without leaking tenancy model into Core?

omar: suggestion: Core exposes "cache_policy_hint": one of {shared, tenant-isolated, pinned}. orchestration maps tenant/hosted constraints to hint. Core implements semantics per hint but does not embed tenant ids.

tanya: from SRE ops: fallback behavior must be explicit. if Orchestration can't satisfy a hint (eg pinned not available), Core should return a capability error code and the orchestration will decide fallback (eg route to different pool or degrade to shared). avoid implicit silent fallback.

liz: good point. add explicit error codes: CAPABILITY_MISMATCH, AUTH_REQUIRED, MODEL_MISMATCH. orchestration handles fallback logic.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary plan template created: https://internal/repo/runtimes/canary-playbooks/decoupling-v1.md :thumbsup:

kai: performance tradeoff: we lose some micro-optimizations if orchestration hides kernel prefs. we could add an optional fastpath where orchestration supplies a kernel_hint vector, but Core should validate compatibility.

liz: propose kernel_hint be advisory only. Core can accept it if safe, else return KERNEL_HINT_IGNORED in the response metadata. keep safety first.

omar: testing: we need a small harness that can simulate orchestration behavior (auth proxies, manifest translations) so we can run cross-env tests in CI. call it adapter-faker. it should be used in unit + integration tests.

maria: also add a tiny perf smoke test that exercises seq_len distribution; we've seen regressions when kernel choices change. include it in premerge for runtime.

tanya: telemetry: ensure we tag traces with "handshake_version" and "cache_policy_hint" so rollouts can be correlated with SLO changes.

liz: rollout timeline sketch: week 0–2 spec + tests; week 3 canary on dedicated with adapter-faker in the loop; week 4–6 hosted opt-in customers; week 7 kill legacy path behind feature flag; week 10 remove legacy.

kai: remove legacy after 3 months of zero usage ideally; feature flag + telemetry gating.

omar: migration mechanics: orchestration will run a translator sidecar for existing deployments. we'll provide a config map: 

```
translator:
  mode: proxy
  map_fields:
    qkv_map: legacy_qkv->core_qkv
    auth: legacy_token->agent-token-proxy
```

maria: are we comfortable with 6 months compatibility? some private customers are slow. maybe keep translator available longer for Private installs but warn it's deprecated.

liz: yep, plan to keep translator binaries available for Private (backport channel) until customer migration is confirmed. hosted/dedicated will have stricter removal.

tanya: ops runbook bits: if CAPABILITY_MISMATCH spikes, automatic rollback policy: 1) disable new handshake at orchestration, 2) route traffic to legacy adapter, 3) open pager if > 1% errors for 10 minutes.

kai: last item: versioning. handshake proto must include a required "handshake_version" field and be backward-tolerant. use semantic-major in the version string (eg "v1" then "v2" requires translator).

liz: thanks all — i'll update the sketch and open RFC with the compatibility matrix and test harness TOC. if anyone has strong objections call them out here, otherwise i'll file tomorrow. :nerd_face:

omar: no objections from infra side. add a short blurb about migration telemetry to the RFC.

maria: fine with me. add a note to contact ML infra customers so we can schedule migration windows.

tanya: sgtm. will add runbook snippets.

infra-bot: reminder: channel retention = 90d. archive related artifacts in the RFC repo.
